findings.body: Ruby replaces the preceding downsize definition with this later definition rather than overloading it, so the job raises ArgumentError for five arguments and emoji files are not resized.
findings.failure_mode: Background emoji resizing fails at runtime due to an arity mismatch.
findings.impact: Ruby replaces the preceding downsize definition with this later definition rather than overloading it, so the job raises ArgumentError for five arguments and emoji files are not resized.
findings.root_cause: A second Ruby class method with the same name redefines, rather than overloads, the existing five-argument downsize method.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a distinct method name for the percentage/dimensions variant, or implement one compatible downsize signature that accepts both width/height and a geometry string while retaining the existing five-argument call contract.
findings.title: Preserve the five-argument downsize API used by emoji resizing
findings.trigger: When the ResizeEmoji job processes an uploaded emoji, it calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at L149 which redefines the five-argument version at L145. Ruby does not overload; the later definition replaces the earlier one. `resize_emoji.rb:14` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 args, which will now raise ArgumentError since only the 4-arg version exists.

findings.body: The browser accepts and uploads an attachment that the server-side UploadValidator will reject for exceeding max_attachment_size_kb, wasting the upload and replacing the immediate configured-limit error with a later failure.
findings.failure_mode: Client and server attachment validation disagree, causing avoidable failed uploads.
findings.impact: The browser accepts and uploads an attachment that the server-side UploadValidator will reject for exceeding max_attachment_size_kb, wasting the upload and replacing the immediate configured-limit error with a later failure.
findings.root_cause: The type-specific client-side size setting was replaced by one fixed value for both images and attachments.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the 10 MB transport limit only for image uploads that can be downsized; continue to read Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] for attachments.
findings.title: Keep attachment validation tied to the attachment size setting
findings.trigger: A site sets max_attachment_size_kb below 10 MB (the default is 3 MB) and a user selects an attachment, such as a 5 MB PDF.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch at L182 replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with hardcoded `10 * 1024`. For attachments, server still validates against `max_attachment_size_kb` (default 3072 KB per site_settings.yml). Client now allows 10MB attachments that server will reject, wasting upload bandwidth.

raw_findings.body: The browser now permits the image, but the proxy returns 413 before UploadsController can run the new downsize loop, so the advertised automatic reduction does not occur on normally configured deployments.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Oversized images are rejected upstream before the new server-side feature can execute.
raw_findings.impact: The browser now permits the image, but the proxy returns 413 before UploadsController can run the new downsize loop, so the advertised automatic reduction does not occur on normally configured deployments.
raw_findings.root_cause: The accepted incoming image size was raised independently of the documented proxy-size configuration contract.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Introduce and document a separate incoming-image transport limit (and require matching proxy configuration), or perform the reduction client-side; update the max_image_size_kb documentation so it no longer instructs proxies to use the smaller post-reduction limit.
raw_findings.title: Document or configure the larger ingress limit required before server-side downsizing
raw_findings.trigger: A deployment follows the existing max_image_size_kb documentation and configures nginx, Apache, or another proxy with client_max_body_size equal to its 3 MB image setting; a user selects a 5 MB image.

raw_findings.body: FileHelper stops writing once its download limit is crossed but returns the partial tempfile; because the configured validator limit is higher than the resulting roughly 10 MB file, the application can process or store a truncated/corrupt image instead of the requested remote file.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Remote-image imports can lose data silently or create malformed uploads.
raw_findings.impact: FileHelper stops writing once its download limit is crossed but returns the partial tempfile; because the configured validator limit is higher than the resulting roughly 10 MB file, the application can process or store a truncated/corrupt image instead of the requested remote file.
raw_findings.root_cause: The URL-download cap was hard-coded below valid configured image limits, while the download helper returns partial content on overflow.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a limit consistent with the configured incoming image limit, and have FileHelper report an over-limit download as an error rather than continuing with a partial tempfile.
raw_findings.title: Do not silently truncate remotely supplied images at a fixed 10 MB
raw_findings.trigger: An API client supplies a URL for a 15 MB image on a site whose max_image_size_kb is configured above 10 MB.

raw_findings.body: The upload error dialog tells the user that the maximum is 10 MB even though the request was rejected at the smaller proxy limit, giving incorrect guidance and encouraging retries that will fail identically.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The client presents a misleading limit after an upstream upload rejection.
raw_findings.impact: The upload error dialog tells the user that the maximum is 10 MB even though the request was rejected at the smaller proxy limit, giving incorrect guidance and encouraging retries that will fail identically.
raw_findings.root_cause: The 413 fallback message was changed from the site setting to an unconditional hard-coded size.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Display the actual configured ingress limit when it is available, or use a generic proxy/upload-limit error instead of asserting a fixed 10 MB value.
raw_findings.title: Do not report every 413 as a 10 MB limit
raw_findings.trigger: An upstream proxy returns 413 at a configured limit other than 10 MB, for example the existing 3 MB max_image_size_kb proxy configuration.

FileHelper.download (lib/file_helper.rb:16-23) writes until `f.size <= max_file_size` then returns the tempfile without error.
